content: Cynodon dactylon, also referred to as Bermuda Grass, Dog's Tooth Grass, Bahama Grass, Devil's Grass, Couch Grass, Indian Doab, Grama, and Scutch Grass, is a grass species native to regions including North Africa, Asia, Australia, and Southern Europe. Despite its name, Bermuda Grass is not indigenous to Bermuda but is instead an invasive species there. The grass has grey-green blades that are relatively short, typically measuring between 4 to 15 cm in length, with rough edges. Its upright stems can grow to heights ranging from 1 to 30 cm, though in rare cases, they may reach up to 90 cm. These stems are slightly flattened and often exhibit a purplish hue. The seed heads are arranged in clusters of 3 to 7 spikes (occasionally only 2), with each spike measuring 3 to 6 cm in length. Cynodon dactylon possesses a deep and extensive root system. Under drought conditions and in penetrable soil, its roots can extend to depths exceeding 2 meters, although the majority of the root mass is typically found within 60 cm of the soil surface. The grass spreads horizontally along the ground, rooting at nodes that come into contact with the soil, thereby forming a dense mat. It reproduces through seeds, runners, and rhizomes. Growth begins when temperatures exceed 15°C, with optimal growth occurring between 24°C and 37°C (75-99°F). During winter, the grass enters dormancy and turns brown. It thrives in full sunlight, while growth is significantly inhibited in areas of full shade, such as near the bases of tree trunks. Cynodon dactylon is extensively cultivated in warm climates worldwide, particularly in regions situated between 30° south and 30° north latitude. It thrives in areas receiving annual rainfall between 625 and 1,750 mm (25-69 inches), although it can also grow in drier regions if irrigation is available. In the United States, it is predominantly found in the southern half of the country and other warm regions. Its rapid growth and resilience make it a popular choice for sports fields, as it recovers quickly from damage. In warm temperate climates, it is a highly sought-after turf grass due to its ability to withstand heat and drought, conditions under which few other grasses can survive. The grass has a relatively coarse texture, and numerous cultivars have been developed to meet specific turf requirements. However, it is also highly aggressive, often outcompeting other grasses and invading various habitats. This invasive behavior has led to its designation as devil grass by some gardeners. Although Cynodon dactylon is claimed to possess medicinal properties, there is currently no robust scientific evidence to substantiate these claims.
